title: ChatGPT helped me fix a scoring bug in Battle Ball. The goal looked bigger than it actually was.
author: No-Engineering-1387
selftext:
In Battle Ball, the big colored Reactor is supposed to be the goal. But I had shots visibly hit the edge without scoring. The game was checking an invisible line that was narrower than the thing players could see. Passes and loose balls were handled differently, too.  
I used ChatGPT to help trace the scoring paths and switch them to the same contact rule. Now direct shots, wall bounces, and deflections can all score when they touch the opposing Reactor. The ball’s path is checked between simulation ticks so fast shots don’t skip through. Old replays still use the rules they were recorded with.  
The part I’d do differently next time: test an edge hit and a near miss as soon as the goal art goes in. A straight-on shot passed under both versions and wouldn’t have caught this.  
For anyone building a replay-based game: when you fix a simulation rule like this, do you keep the old logic around, or record enough of the match that you don’t have to simulate it again?  
The browser build is at [https://battleball.win/](https://battleball.win/) if you want to see it. ChatGPT helped with development, and I used Meshy for the 3D character models.
